front_matter.title: Standard Model currents of the sixteen channels of a light ray, levels and Sugawara split
front_matter.subject: quantum-fields

extraction.note: Attack on the item "the current algebra along generators" of op.qft-non-abelian-gauge-fields: the embedding of the gauge algebra in the u(16) channel currents of a light ray and generation, the levels, and the Sugawara split of the energy along a generator. Stored and used: the pair currents of the channels and their exact window commutator with the level-one central term on edge-clean vectors (synthesis.null-plane-photon-data-and-the-pair-currents-of-the-generators (iv), (v)), the domain D of finite excitations of the band of the null vacuum and the localisation argument of synthesis.exact-window-sugawara-identity-and-luttinger-normal-modes-of-tower-density-waves (iii), the sixteen Weyl components per light ray and generation (synthesis.slot-module-light-ray-arrays-are-weyl-components (ii)), the slot module with its gauge action and the anomaly-free halving (synthesis.cpt-closure-forces-slot-module-and-chirality), the chirality weights about the generator (synthesis.light-ray-good-part-of-a-spinor-is-two-chirality-arrays (iv)), the gauge algebra of the minimal massive composite (standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-massive-composite). Complex or real: each channel is one tower mode per level, a complex fermion with the kernel unit J of the tower level as the scalar of operators (unit principle U2, as in the stored pair currents); the gauge generators are number-conserving on V_+, so they lie in the u(16) of pair currents and need none of the pairing bilinears that enlarge it to so(32). Prior art, not premises: affine Lie algebras and their levels (V. G. Kac, 1968; R. V. Moody, 1968; cited from memory), the Sugawara construction (H. Sugawara, Phys. Rev. 170 (1968) 1659, cited from memory), the coset construction (P. Goddard, A. Kent and D. Olive, Phys. Lett. B 152 (1985) 88, cited from memory), free-fermion current algebras (I. B. Frenkel and V. G. Kac, 1980; P. Goddard and D. Olive, Int. J. Mod. Phys. A 1 (1986) 303; cited from memory); None of these is used: every statement is derived here from the stored window algebra, and the levels, adjoint Casimirs and central values are computed exactly. New to the store: the embedding and the trace identity tr_16 = 4 tr_5 + 4 tr tr on gl(5) (clauses (i), (ii)); the split, with the window condition under which it holds (iii); the level-two values (iv). Ledger: (ii) to (iv) are transport-absent as algebra (free-fermion current algebra on the CAR algebra of tower planes); (i) is transport-convenient (the channels are the series' slot module on the light rays of a horizon). What is not claimed: the Virasoro relations of the factor parts, the transverse dynamics, the four-dimensional gauge field, Yang-Mills, confinement, or a relation between the levels and the cubic anomaly conditions (the levels are quadratic traces; only the trace condition tr rho(Y) = 0 enters, as the vanishing of the hypercharge-number Stored with this one (maintainer pass): the coset part is a function of the so(10) currents, which is why its central value is 52/7 (synthesis.window-energy-of-one-generation-is-exactly-the-so10-sugawara-energy); the embedding and trace form are repeated, as a corollary across the gauge-commuting halvings, in synthesis.light-ray-gauge-currents-of-a-generation-do-not-see-its-anomaly-cancellation. Levels are stated relative to the five-mode trace form, in which hypercharge too is at level 4 (store/conventions.md). central term).

levels.formal:
Let $V = \Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{5}$ be the slot module (modes $1, 2$ the slots, $3, 4, 5$ the pairs; Theorem \claimref{synthesis.cpt-closure-forces-slot-module-and-chirality}), with the gauge algebra $\mathfrak{g} = \mathfrak{s}(\uu(2) \oplus \uu(3)) \cong \su(3) \oplus \su(2) \oplus \uu(1)$ of the minimal massive composite (Theorem \claimref{standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-massive-composite}) acting through the bilinears $\sum_{a,b}X_{ab}a^{*}_{a}a_{b}$, $X \in \mathfrak{g}$, and hypercharge $Y = \mathrm{diag}(\tfrac12, \tfrac12, -\tfrac13, -\tfrac13, -\tfrac13)$, so $Y = (3n - 2k)/6$ on states with $n$ slots and $k$ pairs. Let $V_{+}$ be the half of even mode number (the anomaly-free halving $(-1)^{n + k}$ with the empty state as neutral singlet), and for $X \in \gl(5)$ let $\rho(X)$ be the $16 \times 16$ matrix of $\sum X_{ab}a^{*}_{a}a_{b}$ on $V_{+}$ in the occupation basis. Read the sixteen basis states as the sixteen channels of a light ray of one generation (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.slot-module-light-ray-arrays-are-weyl-components}(ii)): on a window of $L$ levels channel $x$ carries tower modes $c_{x,k}$, $k = 0, \dots, L - 1$ (Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-tower-limit}), $j^{xy}_{m} = \sum_{k}c^{*}_{x,k}c_{y,k+m}$, and for a $16 \times 16$ matrix $M$ with entries in $\mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$ ($J$ the kernel unit of the tower level, $J^{2} = -1$, central among the modes) $J(M)_{m} = \sum_{x,y}M_{xy}j^{xy}_{m}$, $N_{m} = J(1)_{m}$. Let $H = \sum_{x,k}(k + \tfrac12)n_{x,k}$, and let $\Omega_{s}$ fill levels $0, \dots, s - 1$ of every channel. For a subalgebra $\mathfrak{f}$ of $\gl(16)$ on which $\operatorname{tr}_{16}$ is nondegenerate, with a basis $M_{A}$, the trace-dual basis $M^{A}$ and $\lambda_{\mathfrak{f}}$ defined by $\sum_{A}[M^{A}, [M_{A}, X]] = \lambda_{\mathfrak{f}}X$ on $\mathfrak{f}$, put
\[
H_{\mathfrak{f}} = \frac{1}{2 + \lambda_{\mathfrak{f}}}\Bigl(2\sum_{q \ge 1}J(M^{A})_{-q}J(M_{A})_{q} + J(M^{A})_{0}J(M_{A})_{0}\Bigr), \qquad L^{\mathfrak{f}}_{-2}\Omega_{s} = \frac{1}{2 + \lambda_{\mathfrak{f}}}J(M^{A})_{-1}J(M_{A})_{-1}\Omega_{s}
\]
(summed over $A$). Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The embedding.)} $\rho$ maps $\mathfrak{g}$ into $\gl(V_{+})$ (no gauge generator maps $V_{+}$ into $V_{-}$), is a Lie homomorphism, satisfies $\rho(X^{*}) = \rho(X)^{*}$ and $\operatorname{tr}\rho(X) = 8\operatorname{tr}X$, hence is traceless on $\mathfrak{g}$. The compact generators ($X^{*} = -X$, entries in $\mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$) go to anti-Hermitian channel matrices, so the gauge rotations act on the sixteen channels by unitary matrices over $\mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$ and the gauge currents $J(\rho X)_{m}$ are pair currents: they lie in $\uu(16)$ and need no pairing bilinears $c_{x}c_{y}$, $c^{*}_{x}c^{*}_{y}$. All sixteen channels are left-handed Weyl components and carry one weight under the rotation about the generator (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.light-ray-good-part-of-a-spinor-is-two-chirality-arrays}(iv)), so every $\uu(16)$ current, in particular every gauge current, has helicity $0$. The hypercharges of the channels are $0$, $1$ (once each), $\tfrac16$ (six), $-\tfrac23$, $\tfrac13$ (three each), $-\tfrac12$ (two).
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Levels.)} For all $X, X' \in \gl(5)$, $\operatorname{tr}_{16}(\rho(X)\rho(X')) = 4\operatorname{tr}_{5}(XX') + 4\operatorname{tr}X\operatorname{tr}X'$; on $\mathfrak{g}$ the trace form of the channels is four times that of $\C^{5}$. So on window vectors edge-clean at depth $\max(|m|, |l|)$,
\[
[J(\rho X)_{m}, J(\rho X')_{l}] = J(\rho[X, X'])_{m+l} + 4m\operatorname{tr}_{5}(XX')\,\delta_{m+l,0} \qquad (X, X' \in \mathfrak{g}),
\]
and on every window vector the exact window commutator of the pair currents holds. The levels of $\su(3)$ and $\su(2)$, measured by the trace form of their fundamental (the $\C^{5}$ form on each block), are both $4$; for the abelian factor $\operatorname{tr}_{16}\rho(Y)^{2} = \tfrac{10}{3} = 4\operatorname{tr}_{5}Y^{2}$ in the normalisation $Y = (3n - 2k)/6$ (an abelian level depends on the normalisation of its generator; the normalisation-free statement is the factor $4$ between the two trace forms). The three factors are trace-orthogonal and traceless, so their currents commute with each other and with $N_{m}$ on those vectors.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The split.)} $\lambda_{\su(3)} = \tfrac32$, $\lambda_{\su(2)} = 1$, $\lambda = 0$ for $\rho(Y)$ and $N$ (so the coefficients $2/(2 + \lambda)$ are $\tfrac47$, $\tfrac23$, $1$). Define $H_{c}$ by $H = H_{\su(3)} + H_{\su(2)} + H_{Y} + H_{N} + H_{c}$. On the domain $\mathcal{D}$ of finite excitations of the band of the null vacuum in every channel, where $H$ means the sea-normal-ordered $H_{\infty}$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.exact-window-sugawara-identity-and-luttinger-normal-modes-of-tower-density-waves}(iii) summed over the channels and the zero modes $J(M)_{0}$ are counted from the sea, and, with the window $H$ and window zero modes, on window vectors equal to $\Omega_{s}$ outside levels $s - K, \dots, s + K - 1$ when $\min(s, L - s) \ge 3(K + |m|)$, for $X$ in a factor $\mathfrak{f}$ and $X'$ in another factor or $X' = 1$:
\[
[H_{\mathfrak{f}}, J(\rho X)_{m}] = -m\,J(\rho X)_{m}, \qquad [H_{\mathfrak{f}}, J(\rho X')_{m}] = 0, \qquad [H_{c}, J(\rho X)_{m}] = [H_{c}, N_{m}] = 0 .
\]
These relations do not hold on every window vector (they fail on a vector with a particle at the top level of a four-level window): the split into factor parts that generate the factors' own shifts holds on localised vectors only.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Central values.)} For $s \ge 2$, $L - s \ge 2$, $\|L^{\mathfrak{f}}_{-2}\Omega_{s}\|^{2} = \dim\mathfrak{f}/(2 + \lambda_{\mathfrak{f}}) = c_{\mathfrak{f}}/2$ with $c_{\mathfrak{f}} = 2\dim\mathfrak{f}/(2 + \lambda_{\mathfrak{f}})$: $c_{\su(3)} = \tfrac{32}{7}$, $c_{\su(2)} = 2$, $c_{Y} = c_{N} = 1$, and for the whole $\uu(16)$, $L_{-2}\Omega_{s} = \tfrac{1}{34}\bigl(\sum_{x,y}j^{yx}_{-1}j^{xy}_{-1} + N_{-1}N_{-1}\bigr)\Omega_{s}$ with $\|L_{-2}\Omega_{s}\|^{2} = 8$, $c = 16$. The four vectors are mutually orthogonal, each has inner product $\|L^{\mathfrak{f}}_{-2}\Omega_{s}\|^{2}$ with $L_{-2}\Omega_{s}$, and the remainder has $\|L_{-2}\Omega_{s} - \sum_{\mathfrak{f}}L^{\mathfrak{f}}_{-2}\Omega_{s}\|^{2} = \tfrac{26}{7}$: the coset carries $c_{c} = 16 - \tfrac{32}{7} - 2 - 1 - 1 = \tfrac{52}{7}$. The Virasoro relations of the $L^{\mathfrak{f}}$ are not derived; $c_{\mathfrak{f}}$ is defined as $2\dim\mathfrak{f}/(2 + \lambda_{\mathfrak{f}})$, equal to twice the level-two norm, and would be the central charge if they hold.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Reading.} Along each generator, one generation's sixteen channels carry the Standard Model gauge algebra as exact level-four currents (level $\tfrac{10}{3}$ for hypercharge in its own normalisation), of helicity $0$, inside the level-one $\uu(16)$ current algebra, and on localised vectors the energy splits into the factors' Sugawara parts with central values $\tfrac{32}{7}$, $2$, $1$, the number current's $1$ and a remainder $\tfrac{52}{7}$. This is a current algebra along each light ray, kinematics with a $1 + 1$ dimensional energy; it is not the four-dimensional gauge field.
levels.technical:
The sixteen channels of a light ray of one generation are the even-degree states of the five-mode slot module $\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{5}$. The gauge algebra acts on them through number-conserving bilinears, so it embeds in the $\uu(16)$ pair currents of the channels by anti-Hermitian matrices over $\mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$; it never mixes the channels with their conjugates, and since all sixteen channels are left-handed every current has helicity $0$. The trace form of the channels is $\operatorname{tr}_{16}(\rho X\rho X') = 4\operatorname{tr}_{5}(XX') + 4\operatorname{tr}X\operatorname{tr}X'$, so on the gauge algebra the central term of the window current algebra is four times the $\C^{5}$ trace: $\su(3)$ and $\su(2)$ at level $4$, hypercharge with $\operatorname{tr}\rho(Y)^{2} = \tfrac{10}{3}$ in the normalisation $Y = (3n - 2k)/6$.

Splitting the quadratic Casimir of $\gl(16)$ along $\su(3)$, $\su(2)$, hypercharge and the number current, each factor's Sugawara part, normalised by $2 + \lambda$ with the adjoint Casimir $\lambda = \tfrac32, 1, 0, 0$ in the trace-dual basis, generates the shifts of its own currents and commutes with the others' currents on localised window vectors (and on the band of the null vacuum); the remainder commutes with all gauge currents there, but not on every window vector. The level-two norms of the sea give the central values $\tfrac{32}{7}$, $2$, $1$, $1$ and $\tfrac{52}{7}$ for the remainder, out of $16$.
levels.lay: On each light ray at a horizon, one generation of matter supplies sixteen fermion channels, one for each left-handed particle of the generation. Pairs of these fermions form currents, and the forces of the Standard Model act on the channels as rotations of these currents. The strength of the currents' quantum term, the level, comes out as four for both the strong and the weak force, and four for hypercharge when it is measured in the same units as the internal modes. The energy of the channels along the light ray divides into parts built from the currents of each force plus a remainder, whose sizes (central values, the central charges if the factor energies obey the Virasoro algebra, which is not shown here) are computed exactly. This is a theory of currents along each light ray, not the gauge field that fills space.
levels.one-liner: The gauge algebra acts on the sixteen Weyl channels of a light ray by unitary pair-current matrices of helicity $0$ with $\operatorname{tr}_{16} = 4\operatorname{tr}_{5}$ (levels $4$; hypercharge $\operatorname{tr}\rho(Y)^{2} = \tfrac{10}{3}$); on localised window vectors the energy splits into factor Sugawara parts with $\lambda = \tfrac32, 1, 0$ and central values $\tfrac{32}{7}, 2, 1$, number $1$, coset $\tfrac{52}{7}$, out of $16$.

proofs.main:
\emph{Conventions.} The modes $c_{x,k}$ of distinct channels and levels are distinct tower planes, so $\{c_{\alpha}, c^{*}_{\beta}\} = \delta_{\alpha\beta}$ and all other anticommutators vanish (Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-tower-limit}); the check realises them by the Jordan-Wigner signs and verifies the Clifford relations of the planes $e = c^{*} + c$, $f = c^{*} - c$. The unit $J$ commutes with every mode, so $J(M)_{m}$ is linear in $M$ over $\mathrm{span}\{1, J\}$ and $J(M)_{m}^{*} = J(M^{*})_{-m}$, with $M^{*}$ the transpose with $J \mapsto -J$. By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.null-plane-photon-data-and-the-pair-currents-of-the-generators}(iv) and linearity, on every window $[J(M)_{m}, J(M')_{l}]$ is the exact window commutator (the two restricted sums), and on vectors edge-clean at depth $\max(|m|, |l|)$
\[
[J(M)_{m}, J(M')_{l}] = J([M, M'])_{m+l} + m\operatorname{tr}(MM')\,\delta_{m+l,0}, \tag{1}
\]
since $\sum_{x,y,z,u}M_{xy}M'_{zu}(\delta_{yz}j^{xu} - \delta_{xu}j^{zy} + m\delta_{xu}\delta_{yz}\delta_{m+l,0}) = J(MM') - J(M'M) + m\operatorname{tr}(MM')\delta_{m+l,0}$.

\emph{(i)} The bilinears $a^{*}_{a}a_{b}$ conserve the mode number, so they preserve each degree of $\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{5}$ and hence $V_{+}$; this is the action of $S(U(2) \times U(3))$ on $V$ in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.cpt-closure-forces-slot-module-and-chirality}, whose algebra is that of the composite (Theorem \claimref{standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-massive-composite}). The CAR give $[a^{*}_{a}a_{b}, a^{*}_{c}a_{d}] = \delta_{bc}a^{*}_{a}a_{d} - \delta_{ad}a^{*}_{c}a_{b}$, so $\rho$ is a homomorphism; $(a^{*}_{a}a_{b})^{*} = a^{*}_{b}a_{a}$ and the occupation basis is orthonormal, so $\rho(X^{*}) = \rho(X)^{*}$. The diagonal entry of $\rho(E_{aa})$ at a state is its occupation of mode $a$, and $a$ is occupied in $8$ of the $16$ even states, so $\operatorname{tr}\rho(X) = 8\operatorname{tr}X$; $\mathfrak{g}$ is traceless ($\tfrac12 + \tfrac12 - 3\cdot\tfrac13 = 0$ for $Y$). For $X^{*} = -X$, $\rho(X)$ is anti-Hermitian and its exponential is a unitary channel matrix; $J(\rho X)_{m} = \sum\rho(X)_{xy}j^{xy}_{m}$ is a combination of pair currents. The module's numbers are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.slot-module-light-ray-arrays-are-weyl-components}); identifying the occupation basis with the channels carries them to the operators' unit $J$, a matching of units, as for the channel weights in the stored pair currents. By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.slot-module-light-ray-arrays-are-weyl-components} the generation is read as left-handed Weyl fields valued in $V_{+}$, one channel per component, and by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.light-ray-good-part-of-a-spinor-is-two-chirality-arrays}(iv) the rotation about the generator acts on a channel of one chirality by one phase $z$; the mode rotation $U = \prod_{x,k}(1 + (z - 1)n_{x,k})$ multiplies $c^{*}_{x,k}c_{y,l}$ by $z\bar z = 1$ (the computation of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.null-plane-photon-data-and-the-pair-currents-of-the-generators}(iv) with equal weights), so every pair current is invariant. The hypercharges follow from $Y = (3n - 2k)/6$ on the states of degree $0$ ($n = k = 0$), $2$ ($(n, k) = (2, 0), (1, 1), (0, 2)$, multiplicities $1, 6, 3$) and $4$ ($(2, 2), (1, 3)$, multiplicities $3, 2$).

\emph{(ii)} $\operatorname{tr}_{V_{+}}(a^{*}_{a}a_{b}a^{*}_{c}a_{d})$ vanishes unless the operator is diagonal: $a = b$, $c = d$ gives the number of even states containing $a$ and $c$, $8$ if $a = c$ and $4$ otherwise (the even subsets of the other three modes, completed); $a = d \ne b = c$ gives $\operatorname{tr}(n_{a}(1 - n_{b})) = 4$. Hence $\operatorname{tr}(\rho X\rho X') = 8\sum_{a}X_{aa}X'_{aa} + 4\sum_{a \ne c}X_{aa}X'_{cc} + 4\sum_{a \ne b}X_{ab}X'_{ba} = 4\operatorname{tr}(XX') + 4\operatorname{tr}X\operatorname{tr}X'$. On $\mathfrak{g}$ the second term vanishes and (1) gives the displayed relation. On $\su(3)$ and $\su(2)$ the $\C^{5}$ trace is the trace of the fundamental, so both levels are $4$. $\operatorname{tr}_{5}Y^{2} = 2\cdot\tfrac14 + 3\cdot\tfrac19 = \tfrac56$, so $\operatorname{tr}_{16}\rho(Y)^{2} = \tfrac{10}{3}$. Different factors have $\operatorname{tr}_{5}(XX') = 0$ (disjoint blocks, or a traceless block element against a multiple of the identity on that block), and $\operatorname{tr}\rho(X) = 0$, so the central terms between factors and with $N = J(1)$ vanish, and the commutators of the currents of commuting generators vanish by (1).

\emph{(iii), the band.} On the domain $\mathcal{D}$ of finite excitations of the band of the null vacuum in every channel (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.fluctuation-forms-of-the-tower-and-density-wave-bosons-of-the-null-vacuum}(vi), Theorem \claimref{synthesis.null-vacuum-on-a-horizon-generator}(ii)), with zero modes counted from the sea and $H$ the sea-normal-ordered $H_{\infty}$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.exact-window-sugawara-identity-and-luttinger-normal-modes-of-tower-density-waves}(iii) summed over the channels (finite on each vector of $\mathcal{D}$, and $[H_{\infty}, j^{xy}_{m}] = -mj^{xy}_{m}$ there, each term moving a fermion by $m$ levels), (1) holds on every vector: a vector $\psi \in \mathcal{D}$ agrees with the sea outside a finite set of levels, and as in the proof of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.exact-window-sugawara-identity-and-luttinger-normal-modes-of-tower-density-waves}(iii) the operators involved act on $\psi$ as the window operators of a window around it, at whose edges $\psi$ is clean at any given depth. Let $\mathfrak{f}$ be one factor, $S = \sum_{q \in \Z}{:}J(M^{A})_{-q}J(M_{A})_{q}{:}$ (the positive index on the right; by symmetry of $\sum_{A}M^{A}\otimes M_{A}$ this is $2\sum_{q \ge 1}J^{A}_{-q}J_{A,q} + J^{A}_{0}J_{A,0}$), and $X \in \mathfrak{f}$, $m \ge 1$. By (1),
\[
[J^{A}_{-q}J_{A,q}, X_{m}] = J^{A}_{-q}J([M_{A}, X])_{q+m} + J([M^{A}, X])_{m-q}J_{A,q} - m\operatorname{tr}(M^{A}X)\,\delta_{qm}J_{A,q},
\]
and $\sum_{A}\operatorname{tr}(M^{A}X)M_{A} = X$, so the central terms of $2\sum_{q \ge 1}$ give $-2mX_{m}$. Put $P_{a,b} = \sum_{A}J(M^{A})_{a}J([M_{A}, X])_{b}$; invariance of the Casimir tensor, $\sum_{A}([M^{A}, X]\otimes M_{A} + M^{A}\otimes[M_{A}, X]) = 0$, gives $\sum_{A}J([M^{A}, X])_{a}J_{A,b} = -P_{a,b}$, and with its symmetry $\sum_{A}M^{A}\otimes M_{A} = \sum_{A}M_{A}\otimes M^{A}$ also $P_{b,a} = -\sum_{A}J([M_{A}, X])_{b}J(M^{A})_{a}$; so $P_{a,b} + P_{b,a} = \sum_{A}[J(M^{A})_{a}, J([M_{A}, X])_{b}] = J(\sum_{A}[M^{A}, [M_{A}, X]])_{a+b} = \lambda_{\mathfrak{f}}X_{a+b}$ for $a + b \ge 1$ by (1), with no central term. The noncentral terms are $2\sum_{q \ge 1}(P_{-q,q+m} - P_{m-q,q}) + P_{0,m} - P_{m,0}$, all sums finite on $\psi$. In the second sum the terms $q > m$ are the terms of the first, so what remains is $-2\sum_{q=1}^{m}P_{m-q,q} + P_{0,m} - P_{m,0} = -\sum_{q=1}^{m-1}(P_{m-q,q} + P_{q,m-q}) - (P_{0,m} + P_{m,0}) = -m\lambda_{\mathfrak{f}}X_{m}$. Hence $[S, X_{m}] = -(2 + \lambda_{\mathfrak{f}})mX_{m}$; For $m \le -1$, $S$ is self-adjoint (computed in a self-adjoint basis) and $[S, X_{m}] = -[S, (X^{*})_{-m}]^{*} = -(2 + \lambda_{\mathfrak{f}})mX_{m}$; for $m = 0$ there is no central term and the noncentral terms are $2\sum_{q \ge 1}(P_{-q,q} - P_{-q,q}) + P_{0,0} - P_{0,0} = 0$. So $[H_{\mathfrak{f}}, J(\rho X)_{m}] = -mJ(\rho X)_{m}$. For $X'$ in another factor or $X' = 1$, $[M_{A}, X'] = 0$ and $\operatorname{tr}(M_{A}X') = 0$ by (ii), so $[S, X'_{m}] = 0$. Finally $[H, j^{xy}_{m}] = -mj^{xy}_{m}$ exactly (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.null-plane-photon-data-and-the-pair-currents-of-the-generators}(v), $H$ differing from the level operator by $\tfrac12\hat N$, which commutes with pair currents), so $[H_{c}, J(\rho X)_{m}] = -m J - (-m J) - 0 = 0$, and likewise for $N_{m}$. The values $\lambda_{\su(3)} = \tfrac32$, $\lambda_{\su(2)} = 1$ are computed exactly from the trace-dual bases ($\lambda$ is $2h/k$ in terms of the dual Coxeter number and the level, which are not used).

\emph{(iii), windows.} Call a window vector $j$-local if it equals $\Omega_{s}$ outside levels $s - j, \dots, s + j - 1$. On a $j$-local vector, $J(M)_{q}$ with $q \ge 1$ vanishes for $q \ge 2j$ (a fermion must drop onto an empty level, and both lie in the band of width $2j$) and otherwise gives a $j$-local vector, and $J(M)_{-q}$ gives a $(j + q)$-local one; a window operator $J(M)_{q}$ agrees with the band operator on a $j$-local vector when $|q| \le \min(s, L - s) - j$ (the omitted terms would move a fermion across an edge of the window), and the zero modes differ by $s\operatorname{tr}M$, which vanishes for the gauge factors and for $N$ only shifts $H_{N}$ by a multiple of $N_{0}$, which commutes with every pair current. For a $K$-local $\psi$ and $|m| \le K$, $J(\rho X)_{m}\psi$ is $(K + |m|)$-local, $H_{\mathfrak{f}}$ applied to a $j$-local vector uses only $q \le 2j - 1$ and produces $(3j - 1)$-local vectors, so all operators in the relations act as on $\mathcal{D}$ when $\min(s, L - s) \ge 3(K + |m|)$, and the relations hold. The check verifies them on $\Omega_{6}$ and on $J(E_{1,8})_{-1}\Omega_{6}$ in a window of $12$ levels for one generator of each factor, $m = \pm1$, and exhibits the failure on $c^{*}_{x,3}c_{x,1}\Omega_{2}$ in a window of $4$ levels.

\emph{(iv)} Take a basis $t_{a}$ of $\mathfrak{f}$ with $t_{a}^{*} = t_{a}$ and $\operatorname{tr}(t_{a}t_{b}) = \delta_{ab}$ (the trace form is positive on self-adjoint matrices); the vector $v = \sum_{a}J(t_{a})_{-1}J(t_{a})_{-1}\Omega_{s} = \sum_{A}J(M^{A})_{-1}J(M_{A})_{-1}\Omega_{s}$ does not depend on the basis. For $s \ge 2$, $L - s \ge 2$, the vectors $\Omega_{s}$ and $J_{-1}\Omega_{s}$ are edge-clean at depth $1$, $J(M)_{1}\Omega_{s} = 0$ and $J(M)_{0}\Omega_{s} = s\operatorname{tr}(M)\Omega_{s}$. By (1), $J(t_{b})_{1}v = \sum_{a}\bigl(J([t_{b}, t_{a}])_{0} + \delta_{ab}\bigr)J(t_{a})_{-1}\Omega_{s} + \sum_{a}J(t_{a})_{-1}\delta_{ab}\Omega_{s} = J\bigl(\textstyle\sum_{a}[[t_{b}, t_{a}], t_{a}]\bigr)_{-1}\Omega_{s} + 2J(t_{b})_{-1}\Omega_{s} = (2 + \lambda_{\mathfrak{f}})J(t_{b})_{-1}\Omega_{s}$, and $\|J(t_{b})_{-1}\Omega_{s}\|^{2} = \operatorname{tr}t_{b}^{2} = 1$. So $\|v\|^{2} = \sum_{b}\ip{J(t_{b})_{-1}\Omega_{s}}{J(t_{b})_{1}v} = (2 + \lambda_{\mathfrak{f}})\dim\mathfrak{f}$ and $\|L^{\mathfrak{f}}_{-2}\Omega_{s}\|^{2} = \dim\mathfrak{f}/(2 + \lambda_{\mathfrak{f}})$. For $t_{b}$ in another factor the same computation gives $J(t_{b})_{1}v = 0$ (commuting, trace-orthogonal), hence orthogonality.
